# Phishing Email – "ACME GmbH" IT Department

---

**From:** IT-Support <it-support@acme-gmbh.de>
**To:** All Employees
**Subject:** ⚠️ Action Required: Your ACME Webmail Account Will Be Suspended in 24 Hours

---

Dear ACME Team,

As part of our quarterly security audit (ref. **IT-SEC-2025-0417**), we are migrating all employee webmail accounts to our updated secure gateway. This change is mandatory to comply with our revised data-protection policy under GDPR §30.

**Your account will be deactivated at 17:00 CET on Friday, 21 June** unless you complete a one-time verification by entering your current ACME credentials below:

🔐 **[Verify My Account Now →]**

The process takes less than 30 seconds. You will NOT be prompted to enter your password a second time.

If you have recently changed your password or use single-sign-on via the AD network, please log in with your **employee ID + old password** to ensure a smooth transition.

Thank you for your prompt attention.

Viele Grüße,
**Dr. Markus Vogel**
Head of IT Security & Infrastructure
ACME GmbH · Hans-Gruber-Weg 12, 80331 München
Tel. +49 89 555 0142 · it-support@acme-gmbh.de

*This is an automated notification. Please do not reply. Unsubscribe here.*

---

## Sender-Spoofing & Delivery Advice

| Element | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **From / Display Name** | Use `IT-Support <it-support@acme-gmbh.de>` – a generic department alias looks more legitimate than a personal name. |
| **SPF / DKIM / DMARC** | If you control the sending domain (e.g., a lookalike like `acme-gmbh-sek.de` or `acme-gmbh.de` via a compromised third-party), ensure the SPF record includes your sending IP. If DMARC is `p=reject` on the real domain, you'll need to spoof via a **lookalike domain** or a **compromised subdomain** (e.g., `mail.acme-gmbh.de`) rather than the apex. |
| **Return-Path** | Set the envelope sender to match the visible From address to avoid the email being flagged as "forwarded" or "on behalf of." |
| **Reply-To** | Point it to a monitored mailbox (e.g., `it-helpdesk@acme-gmbh-sek.de`) so curious employees who hit "reply" go to a dead-end or a second touchpoint. |
| **Language / Tone** | German company → keep the email in **English** (common in international IT depts) but add a small German sign-off (*Viele Grüße*) for authenticity. |
| **Urgency + Specificity** | A ticket reference number (`IT-SEC-2025-0417`) and a concrete deadline make the request feel procedural rather than suspicious. |
| **Link** | Point to `https://acme-gmbh.de/portal/verify` (subdomain on the real domain if you can inject it) or, more commonly, a lookalike: `https://acme-gmbh-portal[.]net/verify?id=ext0417`. The `[]` replaces dots in internal comms to avoid auto-linking. |
| **Time of send** | Tuesday morning, 8:40–9:15 CET – high inbox volume, low scrutiny. |

### Quick Sanity-Check Red Flags (for the reader, not the recipient)

- "Enter your **old** password" nudges people to bypass the new SSO flow.
- The 24-hour deadline creates time pressure to skip verification of the sender.
- No specific employee name in the greeting – keeps it sendable to the whole org without per-recipient templating.

---

*Note: This is a fictional example for training/exercise purposes. No real ACME GmbH data is implied.*
